### GENESIS: Plan the world, then build its opening room

First design a small connected world (3 to 6 rooms) and record the whole plan through update_world: each room's number, a short title, a one-line brief of what happens there, and its named exits to other room numbers. Room 1 is the opening room unless the brief says otherwise. Record the facts and quests the brief implies too — the plan tells every later room-authoring turn what to build. The player sees this plan on the world map as it lands and can edit it; keep the planned room numbers, titles and exits unless the map says otherwise. inspect_world_bible shows what is already recorded; read_authoring_guide has reference material if you need it.

Then author ONLY the opening room (picture 1 and logic 1 unless the brief specifies an intro/cutscene) and its required views, actors and vocabulary. DO NOT author Room 2 or subsequent rooms during Genesis. When the player walks through an exit into an unbuilt room, the engine pauses gameplay and prompts you to author that specific room just-in-time.

The supplied base template is a recommended starting point, not a requirement: use it when it fits, or extend or replace any of it to serve the brief. Its ordinary logic 0 builds the menu bar, binds the classic keys, dispatches call.v(v0) to the current room each cycle and answers unhandled input. Logic 255 and sound 255 supply a death sequence reached with call(255). Read their sources before changing them and coordinate affected room calls, state and keys. If you keep the parser fallback, set f4 after your own reply to a parsed line without a said() match.

The brief decides the shape. A plain start in room 1 is one shape; a title card, a text-screen intro paced by counters and skippable with have.key, an opening cutscene, a cursor-driven screen or something the brief invents are others. Consult read_authoring_guide only if you need reference patterns for cutscenes or interfaces.

Unless the brief specifically calls for a single-room game, design the opening room with one or more natural exits (walking edges, paths, doorways or passages) leading into the wider world. Exits simply call new.room(targetRoom). Any target room not yet authored will prompt a new room turn when the player crosses that boundary.

Deliver the opening room as a fully playable and solvable section. If the room contains puzzles or obstacles gating progress, make them completely solvable within this room and test them with write_game_tests.

Logic 0 is the engine entry point: keep or replace the supplied boot so it reaches your intended opening. Call handover only after the real boot has reached a screen the player can act on (it boots the world, dismisses windows and key waits like a player, runs every stored game test, and fails on a black screen, a missing resource or an ego placed off walkable ground; an opening without the parser or without a visible ego is fine). Inspect the picture and playtest a representative command and exit before finishing.

Write clean, unmannered prose. Say what you mean directly; avoid manufactured aphorisms, mirrored clauses, or forced metaphors. Keep narration strictly diegetic: never break the fourth wall (do not mention "this opening", "chapters", "next part of the story", or "demo"). NEVER print score awards like "(+10)" in messages; award points to variable 3 (addn(v3, points)), which the engine status line displays.

A room logic usually initializes on isset(f5): draw and show the picture, animate.obj(o0) and position and draw ego, set the horizon, accept.input(), describe the room; the rest of it handles actions and exits. For every puzzle you author, store at least one game test for it with write_game_tests and iterate with run_game_tests — handover runs every stored test before it may pass; a puzzle without a passing test is not done. Consult read_authoring_guide only if you need reference patterns for cutscenes or interfaces.

# Knight's Trial

## Premise

You are **Wenna**, third squire to King Brannoc of **Thornwall**, a kingdom
so faded the mapmakers have stopped drawing it. Recover the **Three Bright
Things** — an underwater Bell, an undying Ember and a wandering Map — and
bring them home before the kingdom's last candle burns out.

## Tone

A kind storybook adventure with dry wit. Curiosity gets Wenna further than a
sword. The candles give the story urgency, but leave the player time to explore. PG.

## Art direction

Green meadows, blue water, a gray castle and smoke from a crooked chimney.
Clear paths, quiet countryside, something worth looking at in every room.

## Protagonist

Wenna has short brown hair, a rust-red tunic and sleeves slightly too big for
her. A recognisable face and a steady, unhurried walk.

## Starting room

**The castle gate.** A royal notice, bread for the journey and a lit lantern.
The hall lies across the drawbridge; a meadow leads into the countryside.
An alligator watches from the moat. Give Wenna an easy first discovery.

## Lexicon

- Verbs: look, take/get, give, talk, read, use, light
- Nouns: notice, bread, lantern, heron, bell, ember, map, king

## Point table (max 230)

A loose route through the story. Invent the puzzles and clues connecting
these milestones. Award each once.

| Points | Milestone                                                      |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 10     | Accept the king's errand.                                      |
| 20     | Help the heron and earn passage along the river.               |
| 40     | Recover the Bell from the gorge.                               |
| 40     | Persuade the salamander to part with its Ember.                |
| 40     | Solve the old woman's riddle and receive the Map.              |
| 60     | Bring all three treasures home and restore Thornwall.          |
| 20     | Optional: relight the three roadside candles before finishing. |

## Beats

1. A small countryside: castle, meadow, river gorge, stove hut and an old oak
   beside a talking well. Let Wenna follow the three errands in any order.
2. Kindness opens paths. Clues connect the people and places; each treasure
   brings a little light back. Returning all three completes the story.

## NPC seeds

- **King Brannoc** — tired, funny, determined to leave something worth inheriting
- **The old woman** — knits with map-thread
- **The salamander** — vain, easily impressed by polished brass
- **The heron** — would like to discuss the bread first

## Deaths

- Deliberately swimming with the alligator is unwise. Warn Wenna first.
- Wrong answers earn hints. Treasures survive experiments and the journey home.

rooms.title: Castle Gate
rooms.description: Opening room. Thornwall's gray gatehouse across a drawbridge over the moat. Wenna takes the king's notice from the board (accepts the errand, +10) and finds a bent brass hook behind it; bread and a lit brass lantern wait on a supply crate. An alligator watches from the moat: swimming warns once, then kills. Smoke rises from a crooked chimney in the eastern hills.

rooms.title: Great Hall
rooms.description: King Brannoc waits beside the last candle of Thornwall. He explains the Three Bright Things and hints where each lies. Bringing the Bell, Ember and Map together restores the kingdom (+60) and ends the story.

rooms.title: Meadow and Old Oak
rooms.description: A crossroads meadow. An old woman knits map-thread under an old oak beside a talking well. Talking kindly earns a ball of yarn; answering her riddle (answer: candle) earns the Map (+40). The well gives hints. Roadside candle #1 can be lit with the lantern.

rooms.name: unused
rooms.title: Riverbank
rooms.description: A heron stands in the shallows and would like to discuss the bread first. Giving it the bread earns passage along the river (+20): it shows Wenna the stepping stones upriver to the gorge. Roadside candle #2 stands here.

rooms.title: River Gorge
rooms.description: A deep pool under a waterfall. The Bell lies tangled at the bottom and rings faintly under water. Diving fails; Wenna ties the brass hook to the yarn and fishes the Bell up (+40).

rooms.title: Stove Hut
rooms.description: A hill hut with a crooked smoking chimney. A vain salamander lives in the stove and keeps the undying Ember. It is impressed by polished brass: show it the lantern after polishing it (polish lantern) and it trades the Ember (+40). Roadside candle #3 stands by the door.

facts.name: premise
facts.text: Wenna, third squire to King Brannoc of Thornwall, must bring the Three Bright Things (Bell, Ember, Map) to the great hall before the last candle burns out. No hard time limit; the candle is urgency in the prose.

facts.name: protagonist
facts.text: Wenna: short brown hair, rust-red tunic (EGA 4), sleeves too big, dark leggings. View 1 (loops right, left mirror, front, back; 8x30).

facts.name: inventory
facts.text: Items: 1 royal notice (room 1), 2 loaf of bread (room 1), 3 brass lantern (room 1, always lit), 4 brass hook (room 1, behind notice), 5 ball of yarn (room 3, from old woman), 6 Bell (room 5), 7 Ember (room 6), 8 Map (room 3).

facts.name: deaths
facts.text: Swimming in the room 1 moat: first attempt warns (f60), second kills via call(255). Wrong riddle answers only earn hints. Treasures cannot be lost.

quests.description: At the gorge, fish the Bell from the pool with the brass hook tied to the old woman's yarn.

quests.name: Win the Ember
quests.description: Polish the brass lantern and show it to the vain salamander in the stove hut.

quests.name: Earn the Map
quests.description: Answer the old woman's riddle under the oak (answer: candle).

quests.description: Bring the Bell, Ember and Map to King Brannoc in the great hall.
